+title: Eight shipped tool rules answer for files they were never given, and eleven leak a temp directory
+---
+Found by the sweep on ^kc0gez9. That card removed both defects from `missing-docs-python.md`. Each sibling rule still holds them.
+
+## Defect 1 — a `files`-scope script given NO file answers for the whole tree
+
+A `files`-scope script judges the files it takes as arguments. Given none, the script hands its tool an empty argument list, and the tool falls back to a default target of its own. The run then answers for every file under the workspace root. It exits 0, so the answer reads as a measured result.
+
+Measured on 2026-08-10. Each script was read out of its shipped rule and run with no argument, in a probe tree that holds one deeply nested file for each language. Each file carries no docstring, one unnamed literal, and 17 branches.
+
+| rule | findings with no argument |
+|---|---|
+| `magic-numbers-swift` | 34 |
+| `magic-numbers-typescript` | 34 |
+| `magic-numbers-python` | 16 |
+| `complexity-python` | 1 |
+| `complexity-swift` | 1 |
+| `complexity-typescript` | 1 |
+| `missing-docs-swift` | 1 |
+| `missing-docs-typescript` | 1 |
+
+Each run exited 0.
+
+Five more rules reported 0 on the same probe, and none of them holds a guard either: `complexity-go`, `function-length-go`, `function-length-python`, `magic-numbers-dart`, `missing-docs-dart`, `missing-docs-go`. The probe tree does not carry the defect each of those reports, so the count is 0 for that reason and not for a guard. Measure each one against a probe that trips it.
+
+`missing-docs-python` is the one rule that guards. It holds `if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then exit 0; fi`.
+
+## Defect 2 — `mktemp -d` with no `trap` leaks a directory on every run
+
+Eleven shipped rules make a temporary directory and never remove it: `complexity-swift`, `complexity-typescript`, `function-length-go`, `magic-numbers-dart`, `magic-numbers-go`, `magic-numbers-swift`, `magic-numbers-typescript`, `missing-docs-dart`, `missing-docs-go`, `missing-docs-swift`, `missing-docs-typescript`.
+
+Three rules already hold the trap, and they are the pattern to follow: `complexity-rust`, `dead-code-rust`, `unused-dependencies-rust`. Each writes `trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT` under its `mktemp`.
+
+Measured on `missing-docs-python` before its trap landed: one run raised the count of directories under `TMPDIR` by 1. After the trap: five runs over one file, and a run that exits 1 on an unparsable file, each leave the count unchanged.
+
+## What to do
+
+- Add the zero-argument guard to every `files`-scope rule that lacks it.
+- Add `trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT` under every `mktemp -d` that lacks it.
+- Prove each behaviour change RED to GREEN with the real tool. Reuse `ShippedEmptyRun` and `verify_shipped_run_reads_only_its_arguments` in `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests/shipped.rs`. ^kc0gez9 added both for the Python probe.
+- State each measurement in the rule body.
+
+The contract now states both traps: `builtin/validators/README.md`, under the `run` key.
+
+#tool-validators #objectivity
\ No newline at end of file

+       a bare `set` over the guard breaks the report. The README words admitted
+       it, so the README changed.

+       DIRECTLY under the assignment, so no statement between the two can exit
+       and leave the directory. The README wrote "under" 1 time and never wrote
+       "directly", so the README changed.

+    Findings 1 and 2 pulled in opposite directions on one constant, and one
+    change answers both: `SHELL_OPTION` (the text `"set "`) is gone, and
+    `sets_shell_options_only` takes its place. A shell option line opens with
+    `set` and it names one option or more. Each word under `set` opens with `-`
+    or `+`, or it is the name a long option takes. A line that holds `--`, a
+    line that holds `;`, `&`, `|`, `$` or a backtick, and a line that names no
+    option each answer false. The README states the same list word for word.
